title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). A 'spatios' Σ is a poset (Σ, ≤) with least element 0_Σ and a complementation C, thought of as an abstract algebra of regions. Disjointness is defined by X |∘| Y iff X ≤ CY. A spatial figure is a pair (Φ, ρ) with:
- Φ ⊂ Σ a family of nonzero, pairwise disjoint regions;
- ρ an order relation on Φ.

This page. Grothendieck lets At_spat(Σ) be the set of elementary spatial figures, those for which (Φ, ρ) has a greatest element. He notes At_spat(Σ) ⊂ At_ens(Σ), the earlier set-theoretic atelier built on the underlying set of Σ. He then puts an 'atelier' structure on At_spat(Σ), i.e. three relations:
1) ◁ is simply restricted from At_ens(Σ).
2) (Φ, ρ) °≪ (Φ', ρ') iff for every X ∈ Φ there is X' = φ(X) ∈ Φ' with X ≤ X', and φ: Φ → Φ' is increasing (for ρ, ρ') and sends greatest element to greatest element. X' is unique: if X ≤ X'1 and X ≤ X'2 with X'1 |∘| X'2, then X ≤ X'2 ∧ CX'2 = 0, contradicting X ≠ 0. So φ is a well-defined refinement map, much like a refinement morphism of partitions or covers.
3) |∘| is made stricter than in At_ens. Let X, X' be the top elements. In At_ens the relation only asks X ≠ X'; here one requires X |∘| X' in Σ. This is stronger because, for nonzero X, X |∘| X' forces X ≠ X'.

He asserts that this gives an atelier, and presumably even a 'spatial atelier'. On the next page he checks Ax1–4 as 'clear'. He then compares with Σ: the top-element map At_spat(Σ) → Σ and the section x ↦ ({x}, trivial order) exhibit Σ as a retract of its atelier of figures, compatibly with |∘|.

The purpose is an axiomatic, order-theoretic theory of configurations of regions ('figures') and their refinements, with a passage between spaces (spatios) and 'ateliers'. It reads like a mereological or synthetic foundation for spatial relations.
errors: The phrase transcribed 'sauf pour X, X' ≠ 0_Σ' must mean 'since/provided X, X' ≠ 0_Σ'. Strictness of X |∘| X' over X ≠ X' uses exactly that elements of figures are nonzero (X |∘| X forces X = 0). Grothendieck's text likely reads 'vu que'.
Uniqueness of φ(X) silently uses an orthocomplement law: X ≤ Y and X ≤ CY imply X = 0. This must be among the spatios axioms, which are not visible here.

Antisymmetry of °≪ is not addressed. With pairwise disjoint nonzero elements it holds only up to equality checks that are not written. The verification of the atelier axioms is merely declared 'clear' (next page).
Nothing ties ρ to ≤ on Σ, so the 'greatest element' is greatest for ρ only. Whether this is intended (a combinatorial labelling of the figure) is not explained.

ideas.what: Elementary spatial figures: families of pairwise disjoint nonzero regions in an orthocomplemented poset, with an order having a top element.
ideas.modern_name: Configurations or partial partitions in an orthoposet / region-based (mereological) structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereology / region-based theories of space (Whitehead, Tarski, Clarke; later mereotopology)

ideas.what: Refinement relation °≪ given by a unique increasing, top-preserving map φ with X ≤ φ(X), uniqueness coming from disjointness.
ideas.modern_name: Refinement morphism of partitions or covers (poset of partitions)

ideas.what: Strengthening the incidence relation |∘| from distinctness of top elements (set case) to disjointness of top regions (spatial case).
ideas.modern_name: Disjointness / orthogonality relation in an orthoposet
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quantum-logic / orthoposet literature (orthogonality X ⊥ Y iff X ≤ Y')

ideas.what: Ateliers: abstract structures (A, ◁, °≪, |∘|) with axioms Ax1–4, and 'spatial ateliers'. Σ is recovered as a retract of the atelier of its elementary figures (next page).
ideas.modern_name: No standard name; closest are region-connection calculi / abstract incidence structures with a representation theorem

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a functorial-looking passage from an abstract 'spatios' (orthocomplemented region poset) to an 'atelier' of figures. He only conjectures that it lands in the subclass of 'spatial ateliers', and leaves the general correspondence between spatios and ateliers open.
missed.quote: Je dis que pour ces relations, on a un atelier, et même (je présume) un atelier spatial.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An unpublished axiomatic theory of spatial configurations by Grothendieck (1986). It parallels mereotopology and qualitative spatial reasoning (RCC-style calculi) without apparent contact with that literature. A specialist in formal ontology or point-free topology might find the representation (Σ as a retract of its atelier of figures) worth comparing with known representation theorems.

missed.claim: Implicit link between Grothendieck's late foundational reflections and region-based, point-free accounts of space (mereology / orthoposets). Here figures are configurations of disjoint regions and refinement is a canonical morphism.
missed.quote: on pose (𝔏,ρ) |∘| (𝔏',ρ') ssi ... non seulement on a X ≠ X' ... mais même X |∘| X'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest; the specific constructions are elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of an apparently unexamined 1986 axiomatic project on 'ateliers' and spatial figures, which is historically interesting. The mathematics on this page is elementary order theory (refinement maps, disjointness) with no deep new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Soit At_spat(Σ) l'ensemble des figures spatiales élémentaires', not 'paires spatiales'. This matches 'figures spatiales' on the previous page.
The script letter rendered 𝔏 is almost certainly Φ, as on the previous page (figures (Φ, ρ)).
'On va mettre une structure d'atelier sur At(Σ)': context suggests At_spat(Σ).
'transforme plus grand élément en id.' means 'en plus grand élément' (idem), i.e. φ preserves the top element.
'(ce qui est plus fort, sauf pour X, X' ≠ 0_Σ)' probably reads 'vu que X, X' ≠ 0_Σ'.
